name: Ancestor Debt — The Genealogy Reparations Pledge
creator: Originated in Tier 3 mutual aid networks; amplified by activist collective Nnaji Futures
description: Participants used their full genealogical and genetic records — newly accessible via consumer BCI ancestry tools — to calculate which of their ancestors had benefited from historical extraction, displacement, or exploitation, then publicly pledged a percentage of their monthly Quanta income to community funds in those lineages. The pledge was not legally binding, but social pressure and feed visibility made non-compliance conspicuous. The trend's viral hook was the discovery, repeated constantly, that nearly everyone's ancestry was both victim and perpetrator at different points, collapsing simple narratives.
medium: neural feed, BCI genealogy tools, public pledge registry
cultural_impact: Ancestor Debt briefly redirected significant discretionary Quanta into Shelf-adjacent community organizations and provoked the first serious public debate in Meridian about whether corponation wealth itself constituted inherited extraction requiring structural remedy.
controversy: Several Tier 4 participants who pledged publicly then quietly reduced or ceased payments were exposed by automated pledge-tracking feeds, generating enormous backlash. Corponation lobbyists successfully argued the trend constituted an unregulated financial instrument and pushed for regulatory oversight of pledge registries.
story_hooks: A character discovers their genealogical record has been altered — someone removed a lineage branch that would have made their Ancestor Debt calculation very uncomfortable.
The community fund where pledge money was deposited has been quietly drained; the fund's administrator has disappeared.
A Tier 5 family's Ancestor Debt calculation, if made public, would implicate them in the founding displacement of the Shelf itself.
